# VERIFY.md — {PROJECT_NAME}

> **Output file location:** project root (`/VERIFY.md`). Tier 0.
> **Purpose:** replaces "□ I checked it" checklists with commands whose exit codes
> are definitive. Agents must not move items to the next column until the relevant
> gate exits with exit 0.

**Principle:** if a rule matters, it must be able to fail automatically.
Rules that exist only in markdown are rules violated silently.

---

## Gate ladder

| Gate | When to run | Who | Kanban column |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gate:fast` | before every commit | agent writing code | In Progress |
| `gate:pr` | before PR leaves draft | agent writing code | In Progress → Testing |
| `gate:qa` | after QA tests are written | qa | Testing → Code Review |
| `gate:merge` | before merge to integration branch | reviewer | Code Review → Ready to Deliver |
| `gate:sit` | before SIT begins | system-integrator | Ready to Deliver → SIT |
| `gate:release` | before production deploy | release | UAT → Release |

Each gate **includes** the gate above it. `gate:pr` runs `gate:fast` first.

---

## Gate definitions

Fill in real commands matching your stack. Leave blank any lines without tooling yet — **do not
write commands that do not exist**, because agents will run them, fail, then fabricate reasons.

```bash
# ── gate:fast ──────────────────────────────────────────────
{pnpm lint}
{pnpm typecheck}
{pnpm test:unit --changed}

# ── gate:pr ────────────────────────────────────────────────
{pnpm test:unit}                  # all unit tests, not --changed
{pnpm test:contract}              # request/response validated against contracts/openapi.yaml
{pnpm lint:boundaries}            # dependency rules from ARCHITECTURE.md §3
{pnpm lint:tokens}                # no hardcoded colors/spacing outside tokens.json
{pnpm build}
{pnpm audit --audit-level=high}

# ── gate:qa ────────────────────────────────────────────────
{pnpm test:e2e}                   # scenarios from acceptance/*.feature
{pnpm test:a11y}                  # axe on changed pages
{pnpm coverage:check}             # thresholds below

# ── gate:sit ───────────────────────────────────────────────
{pnpm test:integration}           # mock ON, all integrations in INTEGRATIONS.md
{pnpm test:contract:live}         # mock OFF, real vendor sandbox — contract diff must be 0
{pnpm db:migrate:dryrun}          # up + down, on staging dump

# ── gate:release ───────────────────────────────────────────
{pnpm db:backup:verify}
{pnpm db:migrate:dryrun --prod-like}
{pnpm smoke}                      # run AFTER deploy, against production URL
```

---

## Numeric thresholds

Numbers, not adjectives. "Adequate coverage" cannot fail; `--lines 70` can.

| Metric | Threshold | Measured by | If failed |
|---|---|---|---|
| Unit coverage (lines) | ≥ {70}% | `coverage:check` | blocks `gate:qa` |
| Critical module coverage ({auth, billing}) | ≥ {90}% | `coverage:check` | blocks `gate:qa` |
| Heaviest route bundle size | ≤ {250} KB gzip | `build` | blocks `gate:pr` |
| Staging LCP (p75) | ≤ {2.5} s | {Lighthouse CI} | blocks `gate:release` |
| Serious/critical a11y violations | {0} | `test:a11y` | blocks `gate:qa` |
| `high`/`critical` vulnerabilities | {0} | `audit` | blocks `gate:pr` |
| Endpoints without openapi.yaml entry | {0} | `test:contract` | blocks `gate:pr` |

---

## What CANNOT be verified by machines

These remain human or reviewer-agent judgment. Separated intentionally so they do not
get mixed with the above — if mixed, agents will treat everything as already
"auto-passed".

Reviewer must answer these six questions on the PR, with sentences, not checkmarks:

1. Is this change actually what the AC requested, or was something done outside scope?
2. Are there variable/function names that would mislead the next reader?
3. Is there an abstraction built for only one consumer (premature)?
4. Were shortcuts taken? Already recorded in `TECHNICAL-DEBT.md` with reasoning?
5. If this feature fails in production at 2 AM, are the existing logs sufficient for diagnosis?
6. Is there a part that only "looks like it works" because the test checks implementation, not behavior?

Quality reference: `references/frontend/anti-slop-core.md`.

---

## Rules for agents

1. **Do not report a gate as passed without running it.** Paste the command output
   (at minimum the summary line) into the PR description or `TASKS.md`.
2. **Gate failed ≠ gate relaxed.** If `coverage:check` fails, write tests — do not
   lower the threshold. Threshold changes require an ADR.
3. **No `--no-verify`, `--skip`, `|| true`, or `continue-on-error`.** If a gate
   must be skipped for a legitimate reason, record in `TASKS.md`: which gate, reason, who
   approved, when it will be repaid.
4. **Skipped tests must have a registered issue.** `it.skip` without an issue reference = violation.
5. **New commands go into this file first, then get used.** If you find a useful check,
   add it to the appropriate gate so it applies to everyone, not just this PR.
